correctness.rationale: The coefficientwise formal identity \(a(N)=\sum_m c_m m!S(N,m)\) is valid. For \(k\ge2\), \(n\ge k+3\), even-base power differences vanish modulo \(2^{k+3}\); the odd-base difference divided by \(2^{k+1}\) reduces modulo four to \(j^{n\bmod2}(j^2-1)/8\). The eighth finite difference \(\Delta^8\) annihilates both parity functions modulo four, so only \(m<8\) contribute. The independently reconstructed coefficient and difference rows have weighted residues \(2\) and \(0\) modulo four. Hence the half-shift is nonzero modulo \(2^{k+3}\) at all sufficiently large even indices, while two half-shifts always cancel, proving least eventual period \(2^k\). Two independent integer algorithms agree on 146 coefficients modulo \(8192\) and on 705 parity-lift tests. The written proof covers every stated parameter.

value.rationale: The sharpness of a newly proved Carmichael-period bound is a natural infinite arithmetic question. Exact least period \(2^{r-3}\) for every \(r\ge5\), with a persistent parity obstruction, is not a finite table extension or a routine implication of the earlier \(\lambda\)-periodicity theorem. The proof isolates a reusable residue profile annihilated by eight finite differences and explains the factor-two reduction.
